title: How Do You Book a TLScontact Appointment?
seo_title: TLScontact Appointment: 7 Easy Steps to Book Your Visa Slot (2026)
desc: TLScontact appointment guide: how to book, reschedule and prepare for a TLScontact visa appointment for France, Belgium and other countries, plus fees and common mistakes.
alt1: tlscontact appointment guide with a passport and travel documents
content:
Short answer: A TLScontact appointment is a booked time at a TLScontact visa application centre, where you hand in your visa documents and give your fingerprints. TLScontact collects applications for several governments, including France and Belgium in many countries. To book a TLScontact appointment, create an account on the TLScontact website for your country and destination, fill in your application, choose a centre and time slot, and print your confirmation. The embassy or consulate makes the visa decision, not TLScontact.

Quick factsDetails
What TLScontact isA private company that runs visa application centres for embassies
Common destinationsFrance, Belgium and others, depending on the country you live in
Who decides your visaThe embassy or consulate
BookingOnline on the official TLScontact site for your country
What to bringAppointment confirmation, passport, form, photo and supporting documents

[IMG1]

What is a TLScontact appointment?

A TLScontact appointment is your time slot at a TLScontact visa application centre (VAC). At the appointment, staff check your documents, scan them, take your fingerprints and photo, collect the fees and send your file to the embassy. They also return your passport when the decision is made.

TLScontact is an outsourcing company. It does not decide visas and cannot influence the result. Its job is to make the collection of applications faster and more organised for the embassy.

Which countries use TLScontact?

TLScontact works for several governments, but which ones it serves depends on the country where you live. Common examples include:

  • France: in many countries, French visa applications go through TLScontact.
  • Belgium: in the UK, Belgian short-stay visa applications go through TLScontact centres in London, Edinburgh and Manchester.
  • Other countries: some embassies use TLScontact in certain countries and VFS Global or BLS International in others.

Always check the official website of the embassy you are applying to. It will tell you whether you need a TLScontact appointment, a VFS Global appointment, a BLS appointment or an embassy appointment.

How do you book a TLScontact appointment, step by step?

Booking a TLScontact appointment takes around 20 to 30 minutes if your documents are ready.

  1. Confirm TLScontact handles your application. Check the destination embassy's website for the country where you live.
  2. Open the official TLScontact website for your destination country and your country of residence.
  3. Create an account with your email address and a strong password, and confirm it from your inbox.
  4. Fill in your application. For France, you usually complete the France-Visas form first and then link it to TLScontact.
  5. Choose your centre based on where you live. Centres cover specific regions.
  6. Pick a date and time for your TLScontact appointment from the available slots.
  7. Print your confirmation and checklist, and keep them with your documents.

What should you bring to your TLScontact appointment?

Bring originals and a set of copies of everything on your checklist. For a short-stay Schengen visa, a typical file includes:

  • Appointment confirmation and the application form, signed
  • Passport valid for at least three months after your trip, with two blank pages, issued in the last ten years
  • Residence permit if you are not a citizen of the country where you apply
  • A recent passport photo that meets Schengen rules (see our visa photo guide)
  • Travel insurance with at least €30,000 medical cover for the whole Schengen area
  • Flight and hotel reservations, or an invitation from your host
  • Bank statements for the last three to six months and an employment or study letter
  • A short cover letter explaining your trip
  • Payment for the visa fee and the TLScontact service fee

How much does a TLScontact appointment cost?

Booking a standard TLScontact appointment is usually free. At the centre you pay:

  • the visa fee, which for Schengen visas is set by the EU (currently €90 for adults, less for children)
  • the TLScontact service fee, which varies by country
  • optional extras, such as SMS updates, courier return, photocopying, form-filling help or premium appointment slots

Premium slots, where offered, cost extra but give more flexible times. They do not make the embassy decide faster.

[IMG2]

What happens at the TLScontact appointment?

On the day of your appointment:

  1. Arrive on time. Late arrivals may be turned away. Allow time for security checks.
  2. Check in with your confirmation and passport.
  3. Document check. Staff check your file against the checklist. They do not judge whether you will get the visa.
  4. Scanning. Your documents are scanned or sent to the embassy.
  5. Biometrics. Your fingerprints and photo are taken, unless you gave Schengen fingerprints in the last 59 months.
  6. Payment. You pay the fees and choose any optional services.
  7. Receipt. You receive a receipt with your reference number for tracking.

How do you reschedule or cancel a TLScontact appointment?

Log in to your TLScontact account and choose the option to change or cancel your appointment. Do this as early as possible, because slots fill up quickly. Rules on how often you can change and whether premium fees are refunded differ by country, so check the terms before you book a premium TLScontact appointment.

What if there are no TLScontact appointment slots?

  • Check early in the morning and at the start of the week, when new slots are often released.
  • Consider a premium slot if one is available and your trip is urgent.
  • Apply early: you can request a Schengen visa up to six months before travel.
  • Avoid websites or people selling appointments; they may be fake and can put your data at risk.

How do you track your application?

After your appointment, use the tracking tool in your TLScontact account or on the website with your reference number. Common stages are "application received", "sent to the consulate", "decision made" and "ready for collection" or "sent by courier". When your passport is ready, collect it or receive it by courier.

TLScontact appointment vs VFS Global vs BLS International

CompanyWhat it doesWho decides the visa
TLScontactRuns visa application centres for embassies such as France and Belgium in many countriesThe embassy or consulate
VFS GlobalRuns visa centres for many governments worldwideThe embassy or consulate
BLS InternationalRuns visa centres, best known for SpainThe embassy or consulate

You cannot choose between them. The embassy decides which company handles applications where you live. Read our BLS appointment guide if your destination uses BLS.

Which TLScontact appointment mistakes should you avoid?

  • Booking at a centre outside your area
  • Choosing the wrong visa type in the online form
  • Missing original documents or signatures
  • Bringing insurance that does not cover the whole Schengen area
  • Arriving late or without your confirmation
  • Paying unofficial agents for appointments

A real example: a TLScontact appointment for France

Leila, an Iranian citizen working as a software engineer in London, wants to visit Paris for a week. She completes the France-Visas form, which gives her a reference number, then opens the TLScontact website for France in the UK and books a appointment at the London centre. She brings her passport, UK residence permit, employer letter, payslips, bank statements, hotel booking, return train tickets and Schengen insurance. The appointment takes 30 minutes. She tracks her application online and collects her passport with a visa nine days later.

Tips for a smooth TLScontact appointment

  • Print the checklist for your exact visa type and use it to order your documents.
  • Bring copies of every page you hand in, in case staff ask for them.
  • Keep a pen and your reference numbers handy.
  • Wear clothing that does not cover your face or ears for the photo.
  • Bring the payment method the centre accepts.
  • For families, book a appointment for each traveller, or a group booking if the site allows it.

How do you book a TLScontact appointment for France?

France uses its own online system, France-Visas, together with TLScontact in many countries. The usual order is:

  1. Find the right visa type with the France-Visas "visa wizard".
  2. Create a France-Visas account and complete the online application.
  3. Print the application form and the receipt with your France-Visas reference.
  4. Follow the link to TLScontact, create your TLScontact account and book your appointment.
  5. Bring both the France-Visas printout and the TLScontact confirmation on the day.

If you skip France-Visas and only book with TLScontact, your file will be incomplete.

How do you book a TLScontact appointment for Belgium in the UK?

UK residents who need a Belgian short-stay visa apply through TLScontact centres in London, Edinburgh and Manchester. You create a TLScontact account, fill in the application, choose the centre for your area and book a appointment. Bring proof of UK residence and the documents on the TLScontact checklist. Our Belgium visa for UK residents guide explains the full process.

Can you get help at the centre?

Many centres offer paid help, such as form filling, photocopying, photos and document checks. These can be useful if you are short of time, but they are optional. They do not change the embassy's decision. Bringing a complete, well-organised file is the best way to make your appointment quick.

Is your data safe with TLScontact?

TLScontact handles applications under contract with the embassy and follows data protection rules. Protect yourself by booking only on the official website, using a strong password, and never sharing your account details with people offering to "help" with your appointment.

How early should you book your TLScontact appointment?

For Schengen visas you can apply up to six months before you travel and at least 15 days before. In busy seasons, such as summer and the weeks before Christmas, book your appointment as soon as your plans are fixed. Leave at least three to four weeks between the appointment and your trip for the decision and passport return.

Key takeaways

  • a appointment is where you hand in documents and give biometrics, not where your visa is decided.
  • Check the embassy website to confirm TLScontact handles your application.
  • Book online, choose the centre for your area, and print your confirmation.
  • Bring originals, copies, Schengen insurance and proof of residence.
  • Never buy appointments from unofficial sellers.

How can Alif Visa help with your TLScontact appointment?

Alif Visa is a UK-registered visa assistance company helping applicants worldwide. We check your documents, help you choose the right visa type, and prepare your file before your appointment. We also arrange travel insurance, flight reservations and hotel bookings. Read our Belgium visa guide, see our visa appointment service, or check your route.

[IMG3]

Frequently asked questions

Is TLScontact the embassy?

No. TLScontact is a private company that collects visa applications for embassies. The embassy or consulate makes the decision.

Is booking a TLScontact appointment free?

A standard appointment is usually free to book. You pay the visa fee and TLScontact service fee at the centre.

Can I reschedule my TLScontact appointment?

Yes, usually through your TLScontact account, depending on slots and local rules.

Do premium TLScontact appointments speed up my visa?

No. Premium slots offer more convenient times, but the embassy's decision time stays the same.

Which countries use TLScontact?

It depends on where you live. France and Belgium use TLScontact in many countries. Check the embassy's website.

Do I need to give fingerprints at every TLScontact appointment?

Not always. If you gave Schengen fingerprints in the last 59 months, you may not need to give them again.

Can someone else attend my TLScontact appointment?

Usually no. You must attend in person to give biometrics, unless you are exempt.

Sources

  • France-Visas (official French visa website)
  • Embassy of Belgium in the UK: Short-stay Schengen visa

title: What Is a Dummy Ticket for a Visa Application?
seo_title: Dummy Ticket for Visa: 7 Easy Facts on Flight Reservations (2026 Guide)
desc: Dummy ticket for visa explained: what a flight reservation is, when embassies accept it, how to get a genuine one with a PNR, and why fake tickets get visas refused.
alt1: dummy ticket for visa guide with a passport and boarding pass
content:
Short answer: A dummy ticket is a genuine flight reservation that you show with your visa application instead of a fully paid ticket. It has a real booking reference (PNR) that can be checked with the airline, but you have not bought the ticket yet. Many embassies, including Schengen embassies, say you should not buy tickets until your visa is approved, so a dummy ticket is normal and accepted. A fake or edited ticket is not a dummy ticket; it can get your visa refused and may count as fraud.

Quick factsDetails
What it isA real flight reservation or itinerary, not yet paid in full
Also calledFlight reservation, flight itinerary, onward ticket
Accepted byMost embassies for visit visas, including Schengen countries
Must haveYour name, flight details and a booking reference you can verify
Never useFake, edited or photoshopped tickets

Table of Contents

  • What is a dummy ticket?
  • Why do embassies accept a dummy ticket?
  • When do you need a dummy ticket?
  • How do you get a genuine dummy ticket, step by step?
  • How much does a dummy ticket cost?
  • Dummy ticket vs fake ticket: what is the difference?
  • What should your dummy ticket show?
  • What if your dummy ticket expires before the decision?
  • Do you need a dummy ticket for every visa?
  • A real example: a Schengen visit to Italy
  • What are the most common dummy ticket mistakes?
  • How does a dummy ticket fit into your whole visa file?
  • What do different embassies say about flight bookings?
  • Airline "hold" options vs travel agency reservations
  • Can you change your dates after the visa is approved?
  • Dummy ticket for onward travel
  • How do you spot a fake dummy ticket service?
  • Hotel bookings work the same way
  • Key takeaways
  • How can Alif Visa help with your dummy ticket?
  • Frequently asked questions
  • Sources
[IMG1]

What is a dummy ticket?

a reservation is a flight reservation made in your name for the dates you plan to travel, without paying for the full ticket. It shows the embassy your travel plan: when you will arrive, when you will leave and which airline you will use. Travel agents and airlines can create these reservations, and the booking normally exists for a limited time.

The word "dummy" is confusing. a reservation should be a real reservation that the embassy can check, not an invented document. Some people call it a "flight itinerary for visa" for that reason.

Why do embassies accept a dummy ticket?

Many embassies tell applicants not to buy non-refundable tickets before the visa is approved. If your visa is refused, you could lose the money. The European Commission's Schengen guidance, for example, asks for proof of travel plans rather than a paid ticket. a reservation solves this: it proves your plan without the financial risk.

When do you need a dummy ticket?

You may need a reservation when:

  • your visa checklist asks for a flight itinerary or reservation
  • you apply for a Schengen, UK, US, Canada or other visit visa and want to show return travel
  • you need proof of onward travel for a visa on arrival or an e-visa
  • an airline asks for proof of onward travel before letting you board on a one-way ticket

Always check your exact checklist. Some embassies accept an itinerary, while a few may later ask for a confirmed ticket before issuing the visa.

How do you get a genuine dummy ticket, step by step?

  1. Decide your travel dates. Match them to your visa application and hotel bookings.
  2. Choose a reliable source. A licensed travel agency, an airline's "hold" option, or a reputable reservation service.
  3. Give your details exactly as in your passport. Name spelling must match.
  4. Get a booking reference (PNR). This six-character code lets anyone check the reservation on the airline's website or through a travel agent.
  5. Check the reservation yourself on the airline's "manage booking" page if possible.
  6. Print it with your name, flight numbers, dates and booking reference clearly visible.
  7. Keep it valid until your appointment. Some reservations expire after a few days, so time it close to your appointment date.

How much does a dummy ticket cost?

Prices vary. Some airlines let you hold a fare for a small fee. Travel agencies may charge a service fee for a reservation. Many people pay a modest amount for a verifiable dummy ticket rather than risking a full fare. Alif Visa's flight reservation service provides reservations for visa applications.

[IMG2]

Dummy ticket vs fake ticket: what is the difference?

Genuine dummy ticketFake ticket
Booking referenceReal, can be checkedInvented or copied
Created byAirline or travel agencyEdited by hand or software
Visa riskNormal, widely acceptedRefusal and possible ban
Legal riskNoneCan be treated as fraud

Embassies can and do check reservations. Submitting a fake document can lead to a refusal, a record on visa databases and, in some countries, a ban on future applications.

What should your dummy ticket show?

A good dummy ticket clearly shows:

  • your full name as in your passport
  • the airline, flight numbers and route
  • departure and arrival dates and times
  • a booking reference (PNR)
  • return or onward travel within your visa dates

If you travel to several countries, the reservation should show the full route, matching your itinerary and hotel bookings.

What if your dummy ticket expires before the decision?

That is normal. Embassies understand that reservations expire. What matters is that it was genuine when you submitted it. If the embassy asks for an updated itinerary, get a fresh reservation. Once your visa is approved, buy your real ticket for the dates on your visa.

Do you need a dummy ticket for every visa?

No. Some e-visas and visas on arrival do not ask for flight proof, and some embassies prefer a simple travel plan. Business travellers may be asked for an invitation letter instead of a strong itinerary. Always follow the checklist for your exact visa type.

A real example: a Schengen visit to Italy

Faisal, a Jordanian citizen living in Dubai, applies for an Italian Schengen visa to visit Rome for ten days. His checklist asks for a flight reservation. He asks a licensed travel agency for a reservation from Dubai to Rome and back, matching his hotel dates. The reservation has a booking reference he checks on the airline website. He submits it with his application. His visa is approved in eight days, and he then buys a real ticket for the same dates.

What are the most common dummy ticket mistakes?

  • Using a website that produces fake tickets with no real booking
  • Name spelling that does not match the passport
  • Dates that do not match the hotel bookings or visa application
  • A one-way reservation when the embassy needs proof of return
  • Reservations that expire weeks before the appointment
  • Buying a non-refundable ticket when a reservation would have been enough

How does a dummy ticket fit into your whole visa file?

a reservation is just one part of your file. Embassies look at everything together:

  • Purpose: your cover letter, invitation or tour plan
  • Money: your bank statements and income
  • Accommodation: hotel bookings or an invitation
  • Insurance: for Schengen visas, Schengen travel insurance with €30,000 cover
  • Return: your job, studies, family or property at home

When all of these tell the same story, your reservation supports a strong application.

What do different embassies say about flight bookings?

Requirements vary, so read your checklist:

  • Schengen countries: usually ask for proof of travel plans, such as a flight reservation, and advise against buying tickets before the visa is issued.
  • United Kingdom: visitor visa guidance does not require a booked ticket; a clear travel plan and dates are enough in most cases.
  • United States: the B1/B2 process does not require a ticket; your DS-160 asks for your intended dates.
  • Some e-visas and visas on arrival: may ask for proof of onward travel at the border or when boarding.

When an embassy does not ask for a reservation, you do not need to add one, but a clear travel plan always helps.

Airline "hold" options vs travel agency reservations

OptionHow it worksThings to check
Airline holdSome airlines let you hold a fare for a short time for a small feeHow long the hold lasts
Travel agency reservationAn agent creates a booking with a referenceThat the reference can be checked
Refundable ticketYou buy a fully refundable fare and cancel if refusedCancellation fees and refund time

All three can work. The key is that your reservation is genuine and matches your plans.

Can you change your dates after the visa is approved?

Yes, within reason. Your real ticket should fit inside the dates on your visa. If your visa allows 15 days from a certain date, travel within that window. Large changes, such as travelling months later, may need a new visa. Short changes within the validity are normal.

Dummy ticket for onward travel

Some countries and airlines ask for proof that you will leave, especially if you fly on a one-way ticket. A genuine onward dummy ticket can satisfy this check. Keep it on your phone and printed, and make sure it is still valid on the day you fly.

How do you spot a fake dummy ticket service?

Be careful with websites that promise an instant "ticket" for a very low price with no real airline booking behind it. Warning signs include:

  • no booking reference, or a reference that does not work on the airline's website
  • a document that looks like an e-ticket but has no ticket number or airline confirmation
  • promises that the document is "guaranteed accepted by all embassies"
  • no company name, address or customer support

A genuine dummy ticket service explains clearly that you are getting a reservation, gives you a reference you can check, and tells you how long it stays valid.

Hotel bookings work the same way

Embassies often ask for proof of accommodation alongside your reservation. Refundable hotel bookings or reservations with free cancellation serve the same purpose. Make sure the hotel dates match your flight dates exactly, and that the names match your passport.

Key takeaways

  • a reservation is a genuine flight reservation, not a paid ticket and not a fake.
  • Most embassies accept a reservation and advise against buying tickets before your visa.
  • Make sure it has a verifiable booking reference and your passport name.
  • Match the dates to your hotel bookings and visa application.
  • Never use fake or edited tickets.

How can Alif Visa help with your dummy ticket?

Alif Visa is a UK-registered visa assistance company helping travellers worldwide. We provide genuine flight reservations and hotel bookings for visa applications, and check that your whole file is consistent. Check your route or talk to us.

[IMG3]

Frequently asked questions

Is a dummy ticket legal?

Yes, if it is a genuine reservation made by an airline or travel agency. Fake or edited tickets are not legal and can lead to refusal or bans.

Do embassies check a dummy ticket?

They can. Embassies may check the booking reference with the airline, so it must be genuine.

How long is a dummy ticket valid?

It depends on the reservation. Many last from a few days to a few weeks. Time it close to your appointment.

Should I buy a real ticket before my visa?

Usually no. Most embassies advise waiting until your visa is approved.

Can I use a dummy ticket for a one-way trip?

For visit visas, embassies usually want to see return or onward travel, so include it.

Is a flight itinerary the same as a dummy ticket?

Yes, the terms are used for the same thing: a genuine reservation used for a visa application.

Can a dummy ticket get my visa refused?

A genuine one is normally fine. A fake one can lead to refusal and future problems.

What if my reservation expires before the embassy decides?

That is normally fine. Officers look at whether the booking was genuine when you applied. Once your visa is approved, buy your real ticket for the same dates if you can.

Do I need a hotel booking as well?

Most visit visas also ask for proof of accommodation, such as a refundable hotel booking or an invitation from your host. Make sure the dates match your flights.

Sources

  • European Commission: Applying for a Schengen visa
  • GOV.UK: Visit the UK as a Standard Visitor

title: What Bank Statement Do You Need for a Visa?
seo_title: Visa Bank Statement: 9 Easy Rules Embassies Check (2026 Guide)
desc: Visa bank statement guide: how many months to show, how much money you need, what embassies check, sponsor statements, sudden deposits and 9 easy rules to follow.
alt1: visa bank statement guide with financial documents
content:
Short answer: A visa bank statement is an official record from your bank showing your name, account number, transactions and balance over a recent period, usually the last three to six months. Embassies use it to check that you can pay for your trip and that your money is genuinely yours. A good visa bank statement shows regular income, a steady balance, no unexplained large deposits, and enough funds for your stay. The exact amount needed depends on the country and the length of your trip.

Quick factsDetails
Usual periodLast 3 to 6 months
FormatOfficial statement, stamped or verifiable, in English or translated
What embassies checkIncome, balance, spending pattern and source of funds
Red flagsSudden large deposits, borrowed money, unclear sources
If someone else paysTheir statements plus a sponsorship letter

  • Why are sudden large deposits a problem?
  • Can someone else's visa bank statement support your application?
  • Savings account, current account or fixed deposit?
  • What if you are self-employed or a business owner?
  • What if you are a student or not working?

[IMG1]

What is a visa bank statement?

A visa bank statement is a statement of account that you submit with your visa application to prove you can afford your trip. It is not a special document; it is your normal bank statement, prepared and presented in a way that answers the embassy's questions. Visa officers read it to understand three things: how much money you have, where it comes from, and whether your finances match the rest of your story.

Why do embassies ask for a visa bank statement?

Embassies want to be sure that visitors:

  • can pay for travel, accommodation, food and activities without working illegally
  • will not become a burden on public funds
  • have a stable life at home and a reason to return

Your visa bank statement is one of the strongest pieces of evidence for all three. A steady salary going in every month and normal spending going out tells a clear story.

What are the 9 rules for a strong visa bank statement?

  1. Cover the right period. Most embassies ask for three to six months. Follow your checklist exactly.
  2. Use official statements. Download them from online banking or ask the bank for stamped copies. Some embassies want a bank letter as well.
  3. Show your name and account number. The account holder must match your passport.
  4. Make sure it is recent. The last entry should normally be within a few days or weeks of your application.
  5. Show regular income. Salary, business income or pension credits each month make your finances believable.
  6. Keep enough balance for your trip, plus a margin for emergencies.
  7. Avoid sudden large deposits. If you must add money, keep proof of where it came from.
  8. Translate if needed. If your statement is not in the embassy's language or English, include a certified translation.
  9. Make it match your story. Your salary should match your employer letter, and your spending should match your lifestyle.

How much money do you need in your visa bank statement?

There is no single figure that works for every visa. It depends on:

  • the country: some Schengen countries publish a daily minimum amount, while others look at your overall situation
  • the length of your trip: a three-day trip needs less than a four-week trip
  • who pays for accommodation: if your host provides free accommodation, you may need less
  • your costs at home: officers look at whether you can still pay your bills while travelling

As a rule of thumb, your visa bank statement should show enough to cover your flights, accommodation and daily spending, with a comfortable margin left over. Check the embassy's guidance for any minimum daily amount.

What do visa officers look for in a visa bank statement?

What they checkWhat a good statement showsWhat raises questions
IncomeRegular salary or business incomeNo income, or irregular cash deposits
BalanceSteady balance that covers the tripA balance that appears only just before applying
SpendingNormal daily costs, rent, billsNo spending, which suggests a "show" account
Source of fundsMoney that matches your jobLarge transfers with no explanation
ConsistencyMatches employer letter and payslipsSalary on the letter differs from deposits
[IMG2]

Why are sudden large deposits a problem?

A large deposit just before you apply is one of the most common reasons for refusal. Officers may think the money was borrowed to make your account look stronger, a practice sometimes called "funds parking". If you received a large amount legitimately, for example from selling a car, a bonus or an inheritance, include proof such as a sale agreement, a bonus letter or legal papers, and explain it briefly in your cover letter.

Can someone else's visa bank statement support your application?

Yes. If a family member, partner or employer pays for your trip, include:

  • their recent bank statements
  • a sponsorship letter explaining who they are, their relationship to you and what they will pay for
  • proof of the relationship, such as a birth or marriage certificate
  • their ID or passport copy, and for some countries, a formal guarantee form

Officers still want to see that you have ties at home, so include your own visa bank statement too, even if your balance is small.

Savings account, current account or fixed deposit?

You can submit more than one account. A current account shows your day-to-day life, which officers like to see. Savings and fixed deposits show additional funds. If you include a fixed deposit, add a certificate showing the amount, start date and maturity date. Do not hide your main account and submit only a savings account with a large balance; that looks incomplete.

What if you are self-employed or a business owner?

Self-employed applicants should show:

  • personal bank statements
  • business bank statements, if the business has its own account
  • business registration documents
  • recent tax returns or accounts

The visa bank statement for your business should show regular trading, and your personal account should show money you pay yourself.

What if you are a student or not working?

Students usually include a parent's or sponsor's statements, a sponsorship letter and proof of enrolment. Retired applicants include pension statements. If you are not working, explain how you support yourself, and include the statements of the person who supports you.

Visa bank statement by visa type

Visa typeTypical expectation
Schengen visit visa3 to 6 months of statements, enough for the trip; some countries publish daily amounts
UK Standard VisitorEvidence you can pay for the trip without public funds; officers look at your overall finances
US B1/B2Not always requested in advance, but useful to show at the interview
Canada visitor visaProof of funds such as bank statements, often for the last few months
Student visasSpecific amounts set by each country's rules, often held for a minimum period

Always follow the official checklist for your country and visa type.

A real example: a Schengen visit for a family

Ahmed, a pharmacist in Cairo, applies for a Schengen visa to visit his brother in Germany with his wife for two weeks. He submits six months of his salary account showing regular monthly salary and normal spending, plus a savings account certificate. His brother sends a formal obligation letter and his own statements. Ahmed's cover letter explains that his brother provides accommodation and Ahmed pays for flights and daily costs. The visas are approved because the visa bank statement, employer letter and invitation all tell the same story.

How do you prepare your statements before you apply?

Start getting ready at least three months before you plan to submit your application. This gives your account time to show a natural pattern. Here is a simple timeline you can follow:

  1. Three months before: keep your salary going into the same account every month and avoid moving money around between accounts without a reason.
  2. Two months before: check your balance against your expected trip costs. If it looks low, save steadily rather than adding one big sum later.
  3. One month before: collect supporting papers such as payslips, an employer letter, tax returns and any proof of large deposits.
  4. One week before: download or collect the latest statements so they are recent on the day you apply.
  5. On the day: print every page in order, including blank or summary pages, and keep a copy for yourself.

Officers often compare your documents side by side, so a calm and consistent record is far more convincing than a balance that jumps suddenly.

What does a bank letter add?

Some embassies ask for a separate letter from your bank, sometimes called a balance certificate or bank reference letter. It usually confirms:

  • your full name and account number
  • the date the account was opened
  • the current balance on a given date
  • the average balance over recent months

A bank letter is useful because it is signed by the bank and hard to fake. If your checklist asks for one, request it a few days before you apply so the date is recent. If it does not ask, adding one is optional but can still help if your account history is short.

How do officers verify what you submit?

Visa officers can and sometimes do contact banks to check that statements are genuine. Many embassies also use specialist teams that look for altered documents, fake stamps and copied formats. Submitting a false or edited document can lead to refusal and, in many countries, a ban on future applications. Always submit your real records, even if they are not perfect, and explain anything unusual honestly in your cover letter.

What if your account history is short?

If you opened your account recently, for example after moving house or changing jobs, explain this in your cover letter. Include statements from your previous account if you still have access to them, a letter from your employer confirming your start date, and recent payslips. A short history is not a problem on its own when the reason is clear and your income is genuine.

Which visa bank statement mistakes should you avoid?

  • Submitting screenshots instead of official statements
  • Removing pages or transactions you do not want to show
  • Depositing borrowed money just before applying
  • Statements in another person's name without explanation
  • Salary deposits that do not match your employer letter
  • Statements that are too old by the time you apply

Key takeaways

  • A visa bank statement proves you can afford your trip and that your money is genuine.
  • Show three to six months of regular income and a steady balance.
  • Explain any large deposit with proof.
  • Sponsors add their own statements and a sponsorship letter.
  • Make your finances match your employer letter, cover letter and travel plans.

How can Alif Visa help with your visa bank statement?

Alif Visa is a UK-registered visa assistance company helping applicants worldwide. We review your visa bank statement and the rest of your file before you apply, and point out anything that might raise questions. Read our guide to visa cover letters, check your route, or talk to us.

[IMG3]

Frequently asked questions

How many months of bank statements do I need for a visa?

Most embassies ask for three to six months. Follow the checklist for your country and visa type.

Does my visa bank statement need a bank stamp?

Some embassies accept online statements, while others ask for stamped copies or a bank letter. Check your checklist.

How much money should be in my bank statement for a visa?

Enough to cover your flights, accommodation and daily costs with a margin. Some countries publish a minimum daily amount.

Can I use my parents' bank statement for a visa?

Yes, if they sponsor you. Include their statements, a sponsorship letter and proof of relationship.

Will a large deposit before applying cause a refusal?

It can raise questions. If the money is genuine, include proof of where it came from.

Do I need to translate my bank statement?

If it is not in English or the embassy's language, include a certified translation.

Can I submit a savings account statement only?

It is better to include your main current account too, because it shows your normal income and spending.

Sources

  • Government of Canada: Visitor visa

title: How Do You Write a Sponsorship Letter for a Visa?
seo_title: Sponsorship Letter for Visa: 8 Easy Steps and a Free Template (2026)
desc: Sponsorship letter for visa guide: who can sponsor, what to include, documents to attach, formal guarantee forms in some countries, and a free sponsorship letter template.
alt1: sponsorship letter for visa guide with a letter and pen
content:
Short answer: A sponsorship letter is a signed letter from the person who will pay for some or all of your trip, such as a relative, partner, friend or employer. It tells the embassy who the sponsor is, how they know you, what they will pay for, and for how long. A strong sponsorship letter is short, specific and backed by documents: the sponsor's ID, proof of their income or bank statements, and proof of your relationship. Some countries also require a formal guarantee form instead of, or as well as, a letter.

Quick factsDetails
Who writes itThe person or company paying for your trip
What it coversWho pays, for what, for how long, and the relationship
AttachSponsor's ID, bank statements or payslips, proof of relationship
Formal formsSome countries use official guarantee forms
Signed?Yes, with date and contact details

[IMG1]

What is a sponsorship letter for a visa?

A sponsorship letter is a written promise from your sponsor to support your visit financially. It might cover accommodation, food, travel, medical costs or everything. Embassies use it to understand why someone else's money is appearing in your application, and to make sure you will not run out of funds during your stay.

A sponsorship letter is different from an invitation letter, although the two are often combined. An invitation says "please come and visit me". A sponsorship letter says "and I will pay for these costs".

Who can write a sponsorship letter?

Common sponsors include:

  • Parents paying for a child's trip, including adult children who are students
  • Spouses or partners supporting each other
  • Relatives abroad, such as a brother or daughter you are visiting
  • Friends hosting you, though embassies may look more closely at their finances
  • Employers sending you on a business trip
  • Universities or organisations paying for a conference or course

The sponsor should have stable income or savings and, ideally, a clear relationship with you.

What should a sponsorship letter include?

A complete sponsorship letter covers:

  1. Sponsor details: full name, address, phone, email, nationality and ID or passport number.
  2. Applicant details: your full name, date of birth and passport number.
  3. Relationship: how the sponsor knows you.
  4. Purpose and dates: why you are travelling and the dates of the visit.
  5. What the sponsor pays for: flights, accommodation, food, insurance, medical costs or everything.
  6. Accommodation: where you will stay and whether it is free.
  7. Assurance: that you will return at the end of your visit.
  8. Signature and date, with a list of attached documents.

How do you write a sponsorship letter, step by step?

Follow these eight easy steps to write a sponsorship letter that works.

  1. Address it to the right embassy or consulate, for example "To the Visa Officer, Embassy of France".
  2. Start with a clear statement: "I, [name], will sponsor the visit of [name] from [date] to [date]."
  3. Explain the relationship in one or two sentences.
  4. List what you will pay for, in plain words.
  5. State where the applicant will stay.
  6. Confirm the purpose and return, briefly.
  7. List the attached documents.
  8. Sign, date and add contact details.

Keep it to one page. Officers read many letters; a clear, specific sponsorship letter is better than a long emotional one.

Free sponsorship letter template

Use this simple template and change the details:

> To the Visa Officer, [Embassy or Consulate] > > I, [sponsor's full name], born on [date], holder of [passport/ID number], living at [address], will sponsor the visit of my [relationship], [applicant's full name], born on [date], passport number [number], from [arrival date] to [departure date]. > > [Applicant's name] will stay with me at [address] free of charge. I will pay for [flights / accommodation / daily expenses / medical insurance / all costs] during the visit. I am employed as [job] at [employer], and I attach my recent bank statements and payslips. > > The purpose of the visit is [purpose]. [Applicant's name] will return to [country] at the end of the visit to continue [work / studies]. > > Attached: copy of my passport/ID, proof of residence status, bank statements, payslips, proof of relationship. > > Signed: [signature] Date: [date] Phone: [number] Email: [email]

[IMG2]

Which documents should you attach to a sponsorship letter?

A sponsorship letter is only as strong as the documents behind it. Attach:

  • Sponsor's ID: passport or national ID, and residence permit if they live abroad
  • Sponsor's finances: recent bank statements and payslips or tax returns
  • Proof of relationship: birth certificates, marriage certificate, photos or messages for friends
  • Accommodation proof: tenancy agreement or property deed if you stay with them
  • Employer letter: for business sponsorship, on company letterhead

Our guide to the visa bank statement explains what officers look for in the sponsor's finances.

Do some countries need a formal guarantee instead of a sponsorship letter?

Yes. Several Schengen countries use official forms that the host signs at a local office:

CountryFormal document (examples)
GermanyFormal obligation letter (Verpflichtungserklärung), signed at the local foreigners' authority
BelgiumGuarantee of support (Annex 3bis), signed at the town hall
FranceAccommodation certificate (attestation d'accueil), obtained from the town hall

These forms are stronger than a simple sponsorship letter because the host formally accepts responsibility. Check the embassy's checklist to see whether your destination needs one.

Sponsorship letter for different visa types

  • Tourist or family visit: focus on accommodation, costs and the relationship.
  • Business trip: an employer letter explaining who pays and the business purpose.
  • Student or short course: a parent or sponsor letter with proof of funds and the course details.
  • Medical treatment: a letter covering treatment costs, with the hospital's estimate.

Does a sponsorship letter guarantee a visa?

No. It helps explain your finances, but officers still look at your whole file. You still need to show that you have reasons to return home, such as a job, studies, family or property. A strong sponsorship letter combined with a weak connection to home can still lead to refusal.

A real example: parents visiting their daughter

Priya lives in London as a nurse with a UK residence permit. Her parents in Kerala want to visit her for a month. Priya writes a sponsorship letter stating that her parents will stay at her flat for free and that she will pay for their flights and travel insurance. She attaches her passport, residence permit, three months of payslips, six months of bank statements, her tenancy agreement and her own birth certificate showing her parents' names. Her parents add their own bank statements and her father's pension letter to show ties at home. Their visas are approved.

How strong do the sponsor's finances need to be?

Officers look at whether your sponsor can comfortably pay for your trip on top of their own living costs. A sponsor who earns enough to pay rent, bills and family expenses with money left over is far more convincing than one whose account would be nearly empty after paying for your flights. There is rarely a fixed figure. Instead, officers compare the sponsor's regular income, savings and outgoings with the likely cost of the visit.

To make this easy to see, the sponsor should:

  • submit three to six months of statements from their main account
  • include recent payslips, a pension letter or tax returns
  • explain any large one-off payment in or out of their account
  • show their own housing costs, for example a tenancy agreement or mortgage statement

If the sponsor is self-employed, they should add business registration papers and recent accounts.

What should the applicant add alongside the sponsor's papers?

Even with a generous sponsor, the embassy still wants to know about you. Add your own documents to show who you are and why you will return:

  1. Your own bank statements, even if the balance is small.
  2. An employer letter confirming your job, salary and approved leave, or a letter from your school or university.
  3. Proof of family ties, such as a marriage certificate or children's birth certificates.
  4. Property or tenancy documents in your home country.
  5. Travel history, for example copies of earlier visas you used correctly.

Together these papers show that the trip is a genuine visit, not a move abroad.

Can a sponsor support more than one person?

Yes. A parent can sponsor two children, or a host can sponsor a whole family. In that case, write one letter listing every person by name, date of birth and passport number, or write a separate letter for each person. The sponsor's finances must be strong enough for everyone travelling, so officers will look more closely at income and accommodation size. If several people stay in one flat, the tenancy agreement or property deed helps show there is enough room.

How should you send the letter to the applicant?

The sponsor can usually sign the original and post it, or sign it, scan it and email a clear PDF. Many embassies accept a printed scan, while some ask for the original with a wet signature. Formal guarantee forms, such as the German obligation letter, normally need the original. Check the checklist and allow enough time for post to arrive before the appointment.

Which sponsorship letter mistakes should you avoid?

  • No signature or date
  • Vague promises such as "I will take care of everything" without details
  • No supporting documents from the sponsor
  • A sponsor with too little income for the trip
  • Dates that do not match the application
  • Using a formal guarantee form incorrectly or not at all when the country requires it

Key takeaways

  • a letter explains who pays for your trip and why.
  • Keep it to one page with clear details and a signature.
  • Attach the sponsor's ID, finances and proof of relationship.
  • Some countries need a formal guarantee form from the host.
  • Show your own ties to home as well; a letter alone does not guarantee a visa.

Frequently asked questions

Who can write a sponsorship letter for a visa?

Usually a parent, spouse, relative, friend, employer or organisation paying for your trip.

Does a sponsorship letter need to be notarised?

Usually not, unless the embassy asks for it. Some countries require a formal guarantee form instead.

Is a sponsorship letter the same as an invitation letter?

No. An invitation asks you to visit; a letter explains who pays. They are often combined.

What documents should the sponsor attach?

Their ID, recent bank statements or payslips, and proof of their relationship to you.

Can a friend sponsor my visa?

Yes, but the embassy may look more closely at their finances and how you know each other.

Can my employer write a sponsorship letter?

Yes, for business trips. It should be on company letterhead and explain the purpose and who pays.

Does a sponsorship letter guarantee approval?

No. Officers still assess your whole application, including your ties to home.
